Q138345.label: Liberal Party of Canada
Q138345.summary: The Liberal Party of Canada is a federal political party in Canada. The Liberal Party espouses the principles of liberalism, and generally sits at the centre to centre-left of the Canadian political spectrum, with their main rival, the Conservative Party, positioned to their right and the New Democratic Party positioned to their left. The party is often described as a "big tent", practising "brokerage politics", attracting support from a broad spectrum of voters.

Q3587177.label: 1949 Jamaican general election
Q3587177.summary: General elections were held in Jamaica on 20 December 1949. Although the People's National Party received more votes, the Jamaica Labour Party won a majority of seats. Voter turnout was 65%. As of September 2020, this election was the last time an independent was elected to the legislature.

Q211561.label: 1978 Belgian general election
Q211561.summary: General elections were held in Belgium on 17 December 1978. The Christian People's Party emerged as the largest party, with 57 of the 212 seats in the Chamber of Representatives and 29 of the 106 seats in the Senate. Voter turnout was 94.8%. Elections were also held for the nine provincial councils and for the Council of the German Cultural Community.

Q6543977.label: Liechtenstein health insurance referendum, 1999
Q6543977.summary: A referendum on health insurance was held in Liechtenstein on 31 January 1999. The proposal, regarding modification of health insurance reimbursements, was rejected by 66% of voters.

Q19360361.label: 2015 Andorran parliamentary election
Q19360361.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Andorra on 1 March 2015. Despite losing five seats, the Democrats for Andorra retained their majority in the General Council, winning 15 of the 28 seats.

Q24169.label: 1998 Czech legislative election
Q24169.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in the Czech Republic on 19 and 20 June 1998. The Czech Social Democratic Party emerged as the largest party, winning 74 of the 200 seats. Voter turnout was 73.9%.

Q7541865.label: Slovenian part-time work referendum, 2011
Q7541865.summary: A referendum on a law on part-time work was held in Slovenia on 10 April 2011. The law was rejected by 80% of voters.

Q5547113.label: Georgi Bliznashki
Q5547113.summary: Georgi Petkov Bliznashki is a Bulgarian politician who served as Prime Minister of Bulgaria in 2014, leading a caretaker government. A member of the Bulgarian Socialist Party, from which he was expelled in 2014, Bliznashki consecutively served as Observer and Member of the European Parliament from 2005 to 2007.

Q110159977.label: 2026 Bulgarian presidential election
Q110159977.summary: Presidential elections were held in Bulgaria on 25 October 2026. Incumbent president Iliana Iotova is eligible and has declared her intention to run for a full term.

Q1633897.label: 1932 Estonian parliamentary election
Q1633897.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Estonia between 21 and 23 May 1932.

Q5450857.label: 1946 Finnish presidential election
Q5450857.summary: Indirect presidential elections were held in Finland in 1946. In 1944 the Parliament had passed a law that enabled Carl Gustaf Emil Mannerheim to serve a six-year term. However, he resigned on 4 March 1946, giving as his reason his declining health and his view that the tasks he had been selected to carry out had been accomplished. An election was held in Parliament to appoint his successor. Juho Kusti Paasikivi was elected with 159 of the 200 votes. Mannerheim had suffered from poor health since 1945, and he had vacationed abroad from November 1945 to January 1946.

Q2009193.label: 2009 attack on the Dutch royal family
Q2009193.desc: event in 30 Apr. 2009, when Karst Roeland Tates drove his car into a royal family parade, killing 8 (including the attacker); the royal family survived
aliases: Dutch royal family attempted ramming attack
Q2009193.wiki: 2009 attack on the Dutch royal family
Q2009193.summary: On 30 April 2009 in Apeldoorn, The Netherlands, a man drove his car at high speed into a parade which included Queen Beatrix, Crown Prince Willem-Alexander and other members of the Dutch royal family. The attack took place on the Dutch national holiday of Koninginnedag.

Q110613097.label: Myanmar Civil War
Q110613097.desc: ongoing armed conflict in Myanmar since the 2021 coup d'etat
Q110613097.summary: The Myanmar civil war began following the military coup on 1 February 2021. The seizure of power triggered mass anti-coup demonstrations and a violent crackdown by the Tatmadaw, which significantly escalated the country's longstanding insurgencies.

Q218217.label: Zoe Lofgren
Q218217.summary: Susan Ellen "Zoe" Lofgren is an American politician and lawyer serving as a U.S. representative from California. A member of the Democratic Party, Lofgren is in her 16th term in Congress, having been first elected in 1994. Lofgren has long served on the House Judiciary Committee, and chaired the House Administration Committee in the 116th and 117th Congresses.

Q184425.label: Pacific War
Q184425.desc: theater of World War II fought in the Pacific and Asia
Q184425.summary: The Pacific War, sometimes called the Asia–Pacific War or the Pacific Theater, was the theater of World War II fought between the Empire of Japan and the Allies in East and Southeast Asia, the Pacific and Indian Oceans, and Oceania. It was geographically the largest theater of the war, including the Pacific Ocean theater, the South West Pacific theater, the Second Sino-Japanese War, and the brief Soviet–Japanese War, and included some of the largest naval battles in history.

Q7876201.label: civil libertarianism
Q7876201.summary: Civil libertarianism is a strain of political thought that supports civil liberties and rights, or which emphasizes the supremacy of individual rights and personal freedoms over and against any kind of authority. It does not refer to economic policy or other aspects of governance typically discussed by libertarians.
